# Labeled Property Graph vs RDF Triplestore Storage Models

> Comparative architecture of Labeled Property Graphs (LPG) with index-free adjacency vs RDF/OWL triplestores with SPARQL and description logics.

## Core Findings

- Labeled Property Graphs store attributes directly on nodes and edges with pointer-based index-free adjacency, allowing O(1) traversal per hop without index scans, whereas traditional RDF stores decompose data into Subject-Predicate-Object triples requiring multi-way index joins. [Source: https://neo4j.com/docs/getting-started/appendix/graph-db-vs-rdbms/]
- RDF engines enforce formal semantics via OWL ontologies and SHACL constraints, providing automated deductive reasoning and global URI disambiguation that standard property graph schemas lack without external validation layers. [Source: https://www.w3.org/TR/owl2-overview/]
- For variable-length path traversal (k > 3), property graphs with index-free adjacency exhibit sub-linear latency growth relative to total graph size, while triple stores encounter combinatorial join-state growth unless path queries are pre-indexed or translated into transitive reachability indices. [Source: https://ldbcouncil.org/benchmarks/snb/]
